subject: Proposal: shifted evaluation window, MAP updates & canary fallback plan
messages:
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hensley <tom.hensley@procureco.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood MAP & security evaluation timing

Hi Soojin / Rishi,

Quick update from our security and procurement teams — they flagged two items that change the evaluation cadence:

1) Security wants an isolated 5-business-day vulnerability scan + audit-log review window that must start during our staging week (they suggested earliest start Jan 10).
2) Procurement needs a signed SOW before we can enable the staging dataset run.

Both of these will push our original close target (Jan 21) unless we adjust the MAP. Can you put together a revised mutual action plan that shows the new gating criteria and a fallback plan if the audit window slips? We also need a short note on how you’ll provide sample audit logs (redacted) — legal insists on scope.

Attaching the security checklist from ACME for reference (ACME-eval-requirements.pdf).

Thanks,
Emily Turner
Director, Platform Partnerships
ACME Corp

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hensley <tom.hensley@procureco.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP & security evaluation timing

Thanks Emily — understood. High level response / proposal:

- We can start the isolated audit-log window on Jan 10 as requested, but to avoid cascading slips we propose splitting work into two parallel tracks:
  * Track A (security gating): full vulnerability scan + redacted audit-log export (we’ll provide a pre-filtered sample set) — target window Jan 10–Jan 14.
  * Track B (procurement + SOW): legal signs SOW in parallel; we’ll share a SOW-draft and can accept DocuSign sign-off to unblock staging.

- Contingency (if security window slips): we will run a controlled canary on a hosted tenant with rate-limited traffic for 48 hours (no production data) and provide post-run artifacts. This keeps the evaluation moving while legal completes the SOW.

Please find a quick MAP sketch attached (MAP_v1.pdf) — it lists milestones, owners, and acceptance criteria.

If you confirm by EOD Friday (Jan 8) we’ll lock the dates and prepare the canary environment. If we don’t get confirmation, our recommendation is to rebaseline close to Feb 04 to preserve capacity and support windows.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP_v1.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: ACME timing impact + escalation threshold

Soojin / Laura — quick internal note before we reply to ACME:

- Security gating Jan 10–14 will likely consume our staging slots; if the audit slips more than 2 business days we should trigger a formal MAP rebaseline and notify Deal Desk.
- I recommend we offer the canary fallback (Soojin suggested) and protect our revenue assumptions by conditioning the current commercial terms on ACME accepting the MAP and SOW by Jan 12. If they miss Jan 12, we propose moving the committed close to Feb 11 and re-evaluating support credits.
- Please confirm whether we can offer a one-time test-credit (5%) to keep momentum if procurement drags. That’s up to you, Laura — flag if you want this elevated to the leadership queue.

If OK I’ll incorporate this language into the external MAP and the updated SOW draft.

—Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hensley <tom.hensley@procureco.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP & security evaluation timing

Soojin — thanks, that proposal is helpful. Procurement will start DocuSign on our side tomorrow but they also asked for:

- A concrete acceptance checklist for the staging run (pass/fail criteria), not just a general MAP.
- Confirmation that the canary will not have access to production logs or PII (we need a short technical note).

Tom from ProcureCo is looping legal to expedite the SOW, but the staging dataset run is blocked until the SOW is signed.

If you can provide the acceptance checklist and the technical note on the canary by EOD Friday (Jan 8), we will aim to sign the SOW early next week. That should preserve close momentum — good faith on both sides.

Emily
Director, Platform Partnerships
ACME Corp
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>, Tom Hensley <tom.hensley@procureco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Revised MAP and mitigation plan (acceptance checklist + canary note)

Emily / Tom — attaching the updated MAP and SOW draft (MAP_v2.pdf, SOW-draft.docx). Highlights below:

- Acceptance checklist (staging run):
  1) End-to-end inference on a 10k-row redacted dataset, 95th pct latency <= 850ms, no PII exposure.
  2) Audit-log export (redacted) delivered to ACME security; schema validated by ACME by day +1.
  3) No critical/high vulns found in the 5-business-day scan.

- Canary technical note:
  * We will provision a dedicated hosted tenant with synthetic traffic for 48 hours. No production user data, no KMS keys shared. Post-run artifacts: telemetry dump, redacted audit logs, and a short runbook showing KV cache usage.

- Revised timeline options:
  Option A (if SOW signed by Jan 12): keep close target Jan 28 with security window Jan 10–14 and staging run Jan 17–18.
  Option B (if SOW or sign-off delayed past Jan 12): rebaseline close to Feb 11 to allow a clean staging and extended QA.

We are flexible on commercial levers but prefer to keep the committed close if ACME signs the SOW on the window above. Please confirm acceptance of Option A or whether you need Option B.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP_v2.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme-corp.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation note & final ask to preserve Jan 28 close target

Emily — looping directly to confirm a final cadence: our team will hold the Jan 28 close target if ACME completes DocuSign for the attached SOW draft and confirms acceptance of the MAP_v2 acceptance checklist by EOD Thursday (Jan 14).

If ACME cannot meet that window we will need to formally move the committed close to Feb 11 to avoid overallocating staging and on-call support. To be explicit: the Feb 11 rebaseline would also shift the committed onboarding support window and could change revenue recognition timing in our internal forecast.

We can offer a one-time 5% evaluation credit to bridge procurement timing, but only if we have a signed SOW and a mutually agreed MAP before Jan 14. This is being offered to preserve momentum, not as a standard concession.

Please confirm whether you accept these terms. If you want me to loop in our Legal / Finance, I can do so — otherwise we’ll await your sign-off.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
Note: internal stakeholders (Rishi / Soojin) — if ACME asks for extended scans beyond Jan 14, I will escalate to the leadership queue and request formal approval for schedule reallocation and any additional credits.
